name: Babe Ruth
hook: Baseball's original home run king — 714 homers, the called shot, and the curse he left behind.

facts.label: the Bambino
facts.statement: George Herman Ruth was nicknamed "the Bambino" — Italian for baby — and also called the Sultan of Swat.

facts.label: sold to the Yankees
facts.statement: The Boston Red Sox sold him to the Yankees for a reported $125,000 in January 1920 — the deal behind the Curse of the Bambino, which lasted until 2004.

facts.label: Red Sox pitcher
facts.statement: Before he was a slugger he was Boston's best left-handed pitcher, holding the World Series record for consecutive scoreless innings from 1918 until 1961.

facts.label: 714 home runs
facts.statement: He hit 714 regular-season home runs, a record that stood until Hank Aaron passed him in 1974.

facts.label: Yankee Stadium
facts.statement: Yankee Stadium opened on April 18, 1923, and Ruth hit its first home run — a three-run shot that beat the Red Sox.

facts.label: the called shot
facts.statement: In the 1932 World Series at Wrigley Field he pointed toward the outfield and then homered — the famous "called shot."

facts.label: $80,000 salary
facts.statement: Told his $80,000 salary was more than President Hoover's, Ruth replied that he had had a better year.
